newsitem.title: CANADA: CBRS reaffirms NOVA unit's debt ratings.
newsitem.headline: CBRS reaffirms NOVA unit's debt ratings.

text.p: Canadian Bond Rating Service said on Monday it reaffirmed the debt ratings of NOVA Corp unit NOVA Gas Transmission Ltd following the approval by Alberta's energy regulator of the pipeline firm's Cost-Efficiency Incentive Settlement.

CBRS said it reaffirmed the ratings of A-1 (Low) and A (Low) on NGTL's outstanding commercial paper and long-term debt securities including Canadian and U.S. shelves and medium note program, with stable outlooks.

The Alberta Energy and Utilities board approval of the five-year agreement between NGTL and its gas shippers showed it would bring in terms of equal sharing of variances on costs and target base earnings, CBRS said.
It will also be a basis to maximize pipeline system use and reduce capital costs for new construction, the rating service said.

"The end result will be a collaborative climate between NGTL, (the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers) and all parties, a streamlined lower toll structure, reduction in new capital spending and greater utilization of the NOVA pipeline system in Alberta," CBRS said.
It said a recently concluded agreement with PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd to avoid the construction of the competing Palliser Pipeline in Alberta also removed an immediate competitive threat.

However, the establishment for PanCanadian and its shipper allies of a "load retention rate" must still be approved by the AEUB and it could also spur other alternative pricing mechanisms with other NOVA customers, CBRS said. ((-- Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
